summary: John Stuart Mill was a philosopher who studied at University College London (~1828–1830). He held a post at the East India Company from circa 1823 to 1858.

John Sydenham Furnivall was a historian who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1896–1900), and Leiden University (~1933–1935). He founded the Burma Research Society in 1910 and held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1936–1941).

John Taber works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his D.Phil. at the University of Hamburg (1973–1979) under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl, later serving at Case Western Reserve University (~1984–1989) and the University of New Mexico (~1989).

John Thompson Platts worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Bedford School and Balliol College, Oxford, he held posts at Benares College (1858, 1861), Saugor High School (1858–1859), and Oxford (1880).

John Vincent Bellezza specializes in Tibetology and archaeology, having studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel. He was affiliated with the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, attested in 2014.

John W. Pettit specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College and doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman, also studying under Dilgo Khyentse, Ashok Gangadean, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

John W. Schroeder specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Los Angeles Valley College and the University of Oregon (Ph.D. 1996) under Don Levi. His posts include the College of Wooster and St. Mary's College of Maryland.
John W. Spellman was a scholar of Indology and history who taught David N. Lorenzen. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1964–1967) and the University of Windsor (~1967–2000).

John Wilson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh (1819–1828). He founded Wilson College, Mumbai, and served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1842) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1869).

John Woodroffe was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at University College, Oxford (~1884–1888) and under Sivachandra Vidyarnava. He served as a Calcutta High Court judge (~1904–1922) and Reader in Indian Law at Oxford (~1923–1930).

Join Saeki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sennyu-ji and under Sadatomo Chihaya. He held posts at Hōryū-ji, the Imperial Academy (1929), and the University of Tokyo, and taught Shoshin Fukihara and Kodo Sawaki.
Joji Fujii is a historian and Japanologist who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1966 to 1974. He subsequently held a faculty post at Kyoto University from circa 1989 to 2011.

Jokai Hiraoka was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He held professorships at Otemae University (attested 1972, 1987) and served at Shuchiin University.

Jon Kabat-Zinn works in religious studies and medicine. Educated at Haverford College and MIT (Ph.D. ~1971), he founded and directed the UMass Memorial Medical Center, held posts at UMass Chan Medical School (~1979–2000), and taught at the Insight Meditation Society.

Jonardon Ganeri is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge and Oxford (D.Phil. ~1994) under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Nottingham, Sussex, Monash, NYU (~2015–2020), and the University of Toronto (~2020).

Jonathan A. Silk is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who earned his doctorate at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez. His posts include Yale, UCLA, and Leiden University, where he became Director in 2007.

Jonathan C. Gold is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He has held teaching posts at the University of Vermont, Drew University (attested 2006), and Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

Jonathan Christopher Cleary was a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies in East Asian Languages and Civilizations at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi and served as an instructor at Wesleyan University.

Jonathan Geen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his doctorate at McMaster University in 2001 under Phyllis Granoff. He has held teaching posts at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover is a philosopher who studied at Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1960–1965). He served as a fellow and tutor at New College, Oxford (~1967–1998) and held posts at King's College London (~1998–2013) and the Hastings Center.
